newsitem.title: USA: ANR says 140 mmcfd gas cut in U.S. Gulf.
newsitem.headline: ANR says 140 mmcfd gas cut in U.S. Gulf.

text.p: ANR Pipeline Co, a unit of Coastal Corp, said Thursday producers shut in about 140 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of U.S. Gulf natural gas production due to Tropical Storm Danny.
"We currently have about 140 mmcfd shut in from about a dozen different blocks. This afternoon we will be evacuating our people from the Eugene Island area block 188," a company spokesman said.

Danny's center was 115 miles southwest of New Orleans and moving northeast at about 5 mph with winds of up to 60 mph. The eye of the storm was expected to make landfall in Louisiana late Thursday or early Friday.

Separately, the National Hurricane Center said Tropical Depression 5, located 12.4 north, 53.4 west or about 475 miles east of the Windward Islands, could become a tropical storm (Erika) later today or tomorrow. TD5 was moving west northwest at 14 mph with sustained winds of 35 mph.
